stem.en: A sponge stays fixed in one place, as a plant does. Why does it not need to make its own food?

text.en: It has green leaves hidden inside its body.

feedback.en: A sponge has no leaves. It is an animal, with pores and water channels.

text.en: Staying still makes every organism eat others.

feedback.en: Staying still does not decide this: a plant stays still too, and it makes its own food.

text.en: It slowly crawls across the rocks in search of food.

feedback.en: Sponges remain fixed in one place. The water moves, not the sponge.

text.en: Water flowing through it brings food to its cells.

feedback.en: Right. Water carries food particles and oxygen to the cells, and carries waste away.

explanation.en: A sponge is an animal and depends on other organisms for food. Water flowing through its pores brings food particles and oxygen directly to its cells and carries waste away.

hints.en: Think about what its pores let in.
